items.desc: The transport federation chair says bookings will depend on road conditions and safer routes for passengers.

items.title: US forces exit Iraq after two decades, leaving an opening for Iran
items.desc: While the eventual departure of US forces is broadly popular among Iraqis, those who worry about the strength of the Iran-backed groups fear the withdrawal is premature.

items.title: Is Nepal’s tourism industry moving fast enough?
items.desc: Nepal’s tourism recovery no longer needs to take years. By shifting from desperate emotional pleas to targeted, transparent digital storytelling, the industry can accelerate its rebound.

items.title: BP Highway reopens after five-day disruption
items.desc: Traffic resumed Tuesday morning on an under-construction permanent track after floods damaged the highway at eight locations.

items.title: Government revives failed plan to separate household and commercial LPG
items.desc: New committee will study separate cylinder sizes and prices for household and commercial users after the latest LPG shortage. Similar efforts in 2011 and 2013 were never implemented.

items.title: Machinery deployed to clear blocked Marsyangdi river in Chame
items.desc: Authorities are widening the river channel to protect homes and a motorable bridge threatened by the rising flow.

items.title: Public Service Commission raises objections to civil service bill provisions, prompting revisions
items.desc: Commission objects to proposed 55-year or 30-year service retirement rule and pension changes, saying they could conflict with legal protections for civil servants.

items.title: Major highways linking Kathmandu reopen after rain disruptions
items.desc: Traffic is flowing on the BP, Prithvi, Kanti, Tribhuvan and Arniko highways, though some sections remain restricted to one-way movement.

items.title: OpenAI shelves new AI model release over safety concerns
items.desc: The ChatGPT maker halted plans for its next-generation model after internal tests found it fell short of safety and alignment standards, including concerns over oversight and disclosure of its actions.

items.title: Bus bookings set to open as Dashain travel approaches
items.desc: Authorities are preparing to reopen damaged roads and ease the annual exodus of around 2 million people from Kathmandu Valley.

items.title: 12 dead in Baglung floods, landslides over past week
items.desc: The deaths occurred over several days as incessant rainfall triggered floods and landslides across the district, destroying 51 houses and damaging dozens of others.

items.title: Foreign minister meets UN General Assembly president, Sri Lankan counterpart
items.desc: Khanal discusses strengthening multilateralism with UNGA president and expanding bilateral cooperation with Sri Lanka.

items.title: US, Iran separately talk with mediators in latest bid to end war

items.title: Welcome tourists back—but build resilient systems to keep them safe
items.desc: The Bhotekoshi flood has once again reminded us that Nepal needs a resilient tourism system to withstand major shocks.

items.desc: Nepal’s quarter-final against Sri Lanka in Nagoya was abandoned without a toss, with Sri Lanka advancing under the tournament’s higher-ranking rule.

items.title: Proposed media law sets penalties from apologies to press pass suspension
items.desc: Simple journalistic errors would draw corrections or apologies, but severe violations could lead to suspension of press passes and state benefits.

items.title: Uproar in Nepal parliament over former chief justice’s unexplained detention
items.desc: Government yet to explain former chief justice’s detention, fuelling questions over the legal basis for the police action.

items.title: All three major Nepal-China crossings hit by monsoon disruptions ahead of Dashain
items.desc: Floods and landslides have halted trade through Rasuwagadhi-Kerung, Tatopani, and Korala border points. Hundreds of containers remain stranded and supplies disrupted ahead of the festive season.

items.title: Malaysia weighs raising minimum wage to RM2,000
items.desc: Any increase would directly benefit eligible Nepali workers employed in Malaysia. About 400,000 Nepalis work in the country.

items.title: Nepal’s broken supply chain: Farmers earn less, consumers pay more
items.desc: Agricultural goods in Nepal pass through up to seven layers of middlemen and this drives consumer prices up to seven times higher than the farmgate price, government report says.

items.title: How visual storytelling is changing the way Nepal experiences cricket

items.title: A four-year-old died of rabies at home last week, but his death does not appear in government records
items.desc: Children are particularly vulnerable to rabies, while misconceptions about puppies can delay lifesaving treatment.

items.title: Rain could end Nepal’s Asian Games medal hopes
items.desc: With no reserve day, Nepal will bow out if rain cancels their quarterfinal against higher-ranked Sri Lanka, a rule coach Stuart Law calls ‘brutal’ for Associate nations.

items.title: eSewa’s new CEO Niraj Sharma on staying ahead in a crowded fintech market
items.desc: Customer engagement, easier and safer payments, cybersecurity and financial literacy will be central to his plans for Nepal’s largest digital wallet.

items.title: Human rights commission summons Kathmandu police chief over Rana detention
items.desc: SSP Santosh Khadka has been asked to explain why a National Human Rights Commission team was denied access to former chief justice Cholendra Shumsher Rana while he was in custody.

items.desc: White House officials had tempered expectations before the summit, pointing ​out that the leaders would also meet at international forums in Shenzen and Miami before year end.
